issues.legal_issue: A valuation register maintained for stamp-duty purposes without statutory foundation cannot establish the market value of acquired land in compensation proceedings.
material_facts: The claimant relied on a register maintained by revenue authorities that recorded values for stamp-duty purposes, including a higher value for commercial property.
No statutory provision or rule authorising the general maintenance of the register as a market-value schedule was identified.
The record contained no other evidence establishing the claimed higher market value.
issues.conclusion: The valuation register could not form the basis for determining the market value of the acquired land.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 4(1) and 23 of the Land Acquisition Act, market value is assessed as of the notification date. The accepted methods include expert opinion, bona fide sale prices for the acquired or comparable nearby land, and capitalisation of actual or immediately prospective profits; comparable bona fide sales are generally preferred. Section 47-A of the Indian Stamp Act, as amended by State legislation, concerns valuation of a particular instrument for stamp duty and does not authorise a general valuation register binding landowners or courts. The Court relied on Special Land Acquisition Officer v. T. Adhinarayan Setty, Tribeni Devi v. Collector of Ranchi, Periyar and Pareekanni Rubbers Ltd. v. State of Kerala, and the reasoning in Sagar Cements Ltd. v. State of A.P.; it also referred to P. Sasidar v. Sub-Registrar, Land Acquisition Officer v. Venkateswara Prasad, Vasireddi Bharata Rao v. Revenue Divisional Officer, and Gulzara Singh v. State of Punjab.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: A court is determining compensation for land acquired for a public purpose.
predicates.valuation_register_is_relied_on: A party relies on a general register of property values to establish the acquired land’s market value.
predicates.register_lacks_statutory_foundation: No statute or rule with legal force authorises the register as a general market-value schedule.

issues.definition: When compensation for acquired land is determined using a general valuation register that lacks statutory foundation, the register is not a basis for the acquisition market value.

issues.legal_issue: An entire undeveloped parcel cannot be valued as commercial land merely because it is near commercial activity when there is no evidence that the parcel was laid out or demarcated for commercial use.
material_facts: The land was in a municipal area with commercial activity nearby and some of it abutted a main road.
The claimant had not prepared or obtained approval for a layout demarcating commercial or residential sites.
There was no evidence, apart from the valuation register, to establish that the whole parcel was available for commercial use.
The whole parcel could not be used as saleable sites without land being set aside for roads and further development.
issues.conclusion: The entire parcel could not be treated as possessing commercial value on the evidence presented.
issues.legal_principle: Market value under Section 23 of the Land Acquisition Act must be established on the evidence and by a method appropriate to the case. A parcel’s possible future use may be considered in an appropriate case, but it does not justify treating the whole parcel as commercial without supporting evidence. Where development is required, land needed for roads and other development purposes must also be accounted for. The Court referred to Section 24, clause sixthly, in discussing future potential use.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: A court is determining compensation for land acquired for a public purpose.
predicates.whole_parcel_claimed_as_commercial: A claimant seeks to value the entire parcel on the basis that it is available for commercial use.
There is no evidence that the parcel was laid out or demarcated for commercial sites.

issues.definition: If the entire parcel is claimed as commercial in a compensation proceeding but no evidence shows that it was laid out or demarcated for that use, the whole parcel is not treated as commercially usable.

issues.legal_issue: Sale documents that are not proved as genuine or shown to concern land with similar advantages need not be relied on to determine market value.
material_facts: The claimant relied on sale deeds executed after the acquisition notification.
No persons connected with those transactions were examined to establish that the sales were genuine or that the land was similar to the acquired land.
The High Court found the relied-on sale agreements to have been fabricated to inflate the claimed value.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was right not to rely on the claimed comparable sales or sale agreements.
issues.legal_principle: Market value may be established through bona fide transactions involving the acquired land or nearby land possessing the same or similar advantages. The transactions must be sufficiently proved to show their genuineness and comparability. The Court also referred to Gulzara Singh v. State of Punjab for the principle that transaction entries in revenue records are not evidence without proof by persons connected with the transactions.

rule.if: land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding and sale_transactions_relied_on and (transactions_not_proved_genuine or comparability_not_proved or agreements_found_fabricated)

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_proceeding: A court is determining compensation for land acquired for a public purpose.
predicates.sale_transactions_relied_on: A claimant relies on sale transactions as evidence of the acquired land’s market value.
predicates.transactions_not_proved_genuine: The parties connected with the transactions do not establish that the sales were genuine.
predicates.comparability_not_proved: There is no proof that the land in the transactions had the same or similar advantages as the acquired land.
predicates.agreements_found_fabricated: The court finds the relied-on sale agreements to have been fabricated to inflate the claimed value.

issues.definition: In a compensation proceeding, transactions relied on as comparable evidence are not relied on when their genuineness or comparability is unproved, or the agreements are found fabricated.

issues.legal_issue: When the State has not challenged the reference court’s compensation award, the claimant’s appeal does not require the appellate court to consider whether that award was excessive.
material_facts: The reference court fixed the market value at a specified rate per square yard.
The State filed neither an appeal nor a cross-objection against that award.
The claimant alone appealed, seeking a higher rate.
issues.conclusion: The High Court did not need to consider whether the reference court’s rate was too high.
issues.legal_principle: In an appeal brought by the claimant seeking increased compensation, the appellate court need not examine whether the award should have been reduced when the State has not appealed or filed a cross-objection.

predicates.claimant_appeal_for_increased_compensati: The claimant appeals a compensation award seeking an increase.
predicates.state_filed_no_appeal_or_cross_objection: The State files neither an appeal nor a cross-objection challenging the award.
predicates.appellate_court_need_not_review_award_fo: The appellate court is not required to consider whether the award should have been lower.

issues.definition: When the claimant alone appeals for increased compensation and the State has not challenged the award, the appellate court need not review the award for excessiveness.
